### Contributing guidelines

- [X] I have read [CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md)

### Module(s)

mini.statusline

### Question

First of all, thank you for the awesome plugin set!

My current issues with `mini`'s statusline (not really `mini`'s issues, but rather my understanding how to configure it to fit my need is still limited at the moment) are

- Is it possible to have only one `mini.statusline` appears on screen while `nvim-dapui` is loaded?

  Here's my `lualine` looks like

  ![nvim-lualine with dapui](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d3300c4e-91e8-483d-a68f-00fab1ae5aca)

  And here's `mini.statusline`

  ![mini.statusline with dapui](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b0eb35d0-0c65-40d9-bc7a-67dfcb2360b9)

- Is there a way to configure only the `filename` section without having to [rewrite](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/blob/4630b9cb783b280fa0fd94e8245d8fb06023f3ba/lua/mini/statusline.lua#L84-L104) entire default [`content.active`](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/blob/main/readmes/mini-statusline.md#default-config).

  In this case I want to only show relative path to current working directory instead of full absolute path. Is that possible?

comment_data.body:
> First of all, thank you for the awesome plugin set!

Thanks for giving it a try!

> * Is it possible to have only one `mini.statusline` appears on screen while `nvim-dapui` is loaded?

The `lualine` screenshot looks like it uses the so called "global statusline". Set `vim.o.laststatus = 3` to have that look. This works with 'mini.statusline' and any other statusline plugin.

> * Is there a way to configure only the `filename` section without having to [rewrite](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/blob/4630b9cb783b280fa0fd94e8245d8fb06023f3ba/lua/mini/statusline.lua#L84-L104) entire default [`content.active`](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/blob/main/readmes/mini-statusline.md#default-config).

I am afraid the suggested way is to indeed define the whole `content.active` as a function. This is an intentional design choice: allow nearly any possible statusline customization at a cost of requiring a significant amount of code for a small change.

Although, technically, there *is* a way with monkey-patching `MiniStatusline.section_filename`. However, this is not a robust solution (as this relies on implementation details which make it work *at the moment*), so I won't provide the actual code or advise to use it.

reply_data.body:
Thank you for your kind response

> it uses the so called "global statusline"

Yes `vim.o.laststatus = 3` did the trick, but then I realized that won't work when I set that option before `require('mini.statusline').setup()`. No matter its using `vim.o`, `vim.g` or even `vim.api.nvim_set_option` like what `lualine` [does](https://github.com/nvim-lualine/lualine.nvim/blob/1517caa/lua/lualine/utils/nvim_opts.lua#L78) neither of them are working.

```lua
require('mini.statusline').setup()

vim.o.laststatus = 3
```

> This is an intentional design choice

That's unfortunate, and I can understand that. Anyway, would you ever consider to have such "section options" for those who really just want a small change, something like 

```lua
require('mini.statusline').setup({
  sections = {
     -- Option: 'full' (default), 'relative', 'filename'
    filename_mode = 'full',

    -- Map existing `diagnostic_levels` to a custom icons
    diagnostic_icons = { 
      ERROR = '',
      WARN = '',
      INFO = '',
      HINT = '',
    }
  }
})
```

Or would you willing to accept it when someone sent you pr in this regard?

reply_data.body:
> Yes `vim.o.laststatus = 3` did the trick, but then I realized that won't work when I set that option before `require('mini.statusline').setup()`.

It does work with any way to actually set the option (which is usually `vim.o`; `vim.g` is for global Vimscript variables), as 'mini.statusline' doesn't change the value [if it is 2 or 3](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/blob/4630b9cb783b280fa0fd94e8245d8fb06023f3ba/lua/mini/statusline.lua#L506).

> That's unfortunate, and I can understand that. Anyway, would you ever consider to have such "section options" for those who really just want a small change, something like
> ...
> Or would you willing to accept it when someone sent you pr in this regard?

I am afraid, this won't happen. The reason for this is that a reasonably sized customization (not a one-off change) on the user side would still get pretty close to writing the full function. The default one is 21 lines and explicitly shows the statusline parts (which is a good thing in my opinion). And that is not even considering the added complexity on 'mini.statusline' code.
